sections.text:
1 Exemplar huius libri invenire non potuit Steinschneider (l. c., p. 371 b), qui
opinatur illum eumdem fere esse atque liber de imaginibus, p. 98, n. 5.
2 Liber lunae sine auctoris nomine apud Arabes laudatur. Cf. Steinschneider,
l. c., p. 372 c.
3 Liber posterior Balenis idem esse videtur atque liber de imaginibus supra p. 98,
n. 4; prior exstare non videtur; cf. Steinschneider, l. c., p. 369, § 18.
4 De Hermetis libris cf. supra p. 98. De illis qui hic enumerantur nihil afferre
potuit Steinschneider, l. c., p. 372 ss.
sections.en:
1 Steinschneider could not find a copy of this book (loc. cit., p. 371 b), who
opines that it is almost the same as the book concerning images, p. 98, n. 5.
2 The Book of the Moon is praised without the author's name among the Arabs. Cf. Steinschneider,
loc. cit., p. 372 c.
3 The latter book of Balenis seems to be the same as the book concerning images above p. 98,
n. 4; the former does not seem to exist; cf. Steinschneider, loc. cit., p. 369, § 18.
4 Concerning the books of Hermes cf. above p. 98. Concerning those which are enumerated here Steinschneider could bring nothing,
loc. cit., p. 372 ff.

summary.headline: Hermetic and Planetary Image Books
summary.text: A catalogue of astrological and magical works attributed to Hermes and Balenis, including the Book of Illusions, Book of the Moon, works on planetary images, and treatises on characters, rings, and seals of Mercury, Venus, and the Sun.
